thread:
ops-bot: ALERT — canary telemetry breach in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for release-2026.03.16. Latency 95p up 2.6x, throughput down 30%, error-rate up. Auto-threshold triggered. Paging SRE.

sre_oncall: Acknowledged. I'm on call. Pulling logs and canary dashboard.

eng_release_lead: Noted. Canary was 5% traffic multi-region. No config changes after deploy besides the new prefetch tuning.

ria: Customer impact: two enterprise tenants (eu-dedicated) reported request timeouts and elevated tail latency. CS alerted.

sam: Observing kernel fallback events in the runtime logs across the canary hosts: `kernel_fallback=true` and batching collapsed (batch_size -> 1). Looks correlated with traffic spikes.

lee: Confirmed. Heatmap shows KV cache evictions around the same time. Prefetch burst + small cache led to thrash.

eng_release_lead: Can we flip the runtime prefetch flag off remotely? If prefetch is causing evictions, that should stop the thrash.

lee: Proposing kill-switch: `feature_flag: inference.prefetch = false` for canary and pause rollout. Command ready.

sre_oncall: Do it. Also reduce canary traffic to 0% and start rollback if latency doesn't recover in 2 min.

eng_release_lead: Executing now.
```bash
# flip flag for canary group
curl -s -X POST "https://internal-api/flags" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"flag":"inference.prefetch","value":false,"scope":"canary"}'
# scale canary down
/internalctl rollout traffic shift --release release-2026.03.16 --to 0.0
```

ops-bot: ACTION: feature_flag change applied (inference.prefetch=false) for canary. Traffic shift started.

sam: After flip: kernel_fallback logs drop, batching resumes to normal sizes, latency 95p trending down but still 1.3x baseline. Throughput recovering.

ria: CS: notifying affected customers with initial impact note, ETA for full restore 15–30m.

csm_olivia: Sent message to customers on the affected list. Will escalate for any critical SLAs.

eng_release_lead: Rolling back the release from the canary pool as a precaution while eng-runtime investigates root cause. Rollback cmd: `/rollout rollback release-2026.03.16 --canary-only` executed.

ops-bot: ROLLBACK: canary rollback completed. Canary traffic 0%. Global stable version remains serving.

sre_oncall: Marking as mitigated for now. Continuing to monitor for 30m. Creating follow-up incident doc and postmortem assignment to eng-runtime + infra.

sam: Adding initial notes: probable trigger: prefetch behavior interacts badly with small KV cache under bursty multi-region canary traffic -> evictions -> kernel fallback -> batch collapse -> tail latency. Needs repro and guardrails (auto-disable prefetch on high-eviction signals).

lee: Will add metric-based kill-switch and a canary config that pins cache sizes for rollouts.

eng_release_lead: Thanks team. Postmortem doc starter: https://redwood-internal/incidents/3529994321. Assigning owners: eng-runtime (sam), infra (lee), release (me).

ops-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. If latency or errors reappear, reopen paging. :white_check_mark:

csm_olivia: I'll follow up with affected accounts once we have the postmortem.

sre_oncall: Handing off to daytime oncall @eng-runtime for deeper investigation. End of active paging.
